items.q: What does terraform plan show and why always read it first?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Shows the diff: + created, - destroyed, ~ modified, -/+ destroy+recreate. A common mistake: renaming an S3 bucket shows -/+ which would delete all data. The plan reveals this before it happens. Equivalent to reviewing a database migration before running it.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Terraform parses HCL into an execution graph, reconciling state file (.tfstate) against remote cloud provider APIs via provider plugins.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Unlocked concurrent state modifications or drift between cloud resources and local state cause resource deletion or corrupt state.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Remote state locking (DynamoDB/S3) ensures safe team collaboration but requires strict CI/CD discipline.

items.q: What is Terraform state and why never commit it?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** terraform.tfstate maps your .tf resource blocks to real AWS resource IDs and often contains sensitive values (passwords, keys). Committing exposes these in Git history. For teams, local state means concurrent applies can corrupt it -- solution: remote state in S3 + DynamoDB locking.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Terraform parses HCL into an execution graph, reconciling state file (.tfstate) against remote cloud provider APIs via provider plugins.

items.q: Why S3 + DynamoDB for remote state?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** S3 stores the file centrally, encrypted, with versioning. DynamoDB adds a mutex: before terraform apply, Terraform writes a lock entry; if another apply is running, it waits. Prevents concurrent applies from corrupting state -- essential for CI/CD and team use.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Terraform parses HCL into an execution graph, reconciling state file (.tfstate) against remote cloud provider APIs via provider plugins.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Unlocked concurrent state modifications or drift between cloud resources and local state cause resource deletion or corrupt state.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Remote state locking (DynamoDB/S3) ensures safe team collaboration but requires strict CI/CD discipline.

items.q: What should a data pipeline Grafana dashboard include?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Records ingested per run/source, job duration trend, error rate, EMR cluster cost/idle time, last successful run time per source. A Stat panel showing last run: 2 hours ago for an hourly job immediately surfaces a missed run.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

**Elevator Pitch:** Dropdown filters at the top that filter all panels simultaneously. $source with values [Bloomberg, ICE] -- selecting one filters every panel. Avoids creating 50 identical dashboards. Interpolated into queries: rate(records{source='$source'}[5m]).

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

items.q: Grafana vs Kibana -- when use each?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Grafana for metrics -- numerical time-series (CPU%, error rate). Best for how is my system performing. Kibana for logs -- event documents. Best for what exactly happened at 3am. A production platform uses both: Grafana for dashboards, Kibana for log debugging.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Message brokers persist events to partitioned append-only logs or in-memory queues, enabling distributed pub/sub with consumer groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Poison pill messages without dead-letter queues (DLQ) block partition processing and trigger infinite retry loops.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Partitioned event streaming (Kafka) guarantees order per key at scale, but partition rebalancing incurs consumer pause latency.

items.q: Why is structured JSON logging better than plain text?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Plain text requires Logstash grok patterns to parse fields -- fragile, breaks on format changes. JSON logs parse automatically; Elasticsearch creates fields with zero config. You can immediately filter level:ERROR AND source:Bloomberg without writing parsing rules.

items.q: What is back-pressure and why does it matter?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A threshold on a Connection queue. When exceeded (10,000 objects or 1GB), NiFi pauses the upstream processor automatically. Without it, a fast producer and slow consumer fill memory indefinitely until OOM. Back-pressure provides implicit flow control.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Message brokers persist events to partitioned append-only logs or in-memory queues, enabling distributed pub/sub with consumer groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Poison pill messages without dead-letter queues (DLQ) block partition processing and trigger infinite retry loops.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Partitioned event streaming (Kafka) guarantees order per key at scale, but partition rebalancing incurs consumer pause latency.

items.q: How would you design a NiFi flow for 50 sources?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Config-driven: each source is a parameter context entry, not a separate Processor set. One generic GetHTTP reads the URL from a parameter; UpdateAttribute adds source name and date; RouteOnAttribute branches valid/invalid; PutS3Object writes to landing zone. Adding source 51 is a config entry -- zero Processor changes.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

items.q: Precision vs recall with a financial data example?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Precision: of companies flagged as likely to default, how many actually did -- high precision means few false alarms. Recall: of companies that actually defaulted, how many did the model catch -- high recall means few misses. Trade-off: increasing sensitivity catches more real defaults but flags more false alarms. The business decides which matters more.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

items.q: What is model drift and why is it a data pipeline problem?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The relationship between features and labels changes over time -- a fraud model trained on 2022 data becomes less accurate as patterns evolve. Requires pipelines that continuously evaluate accuracy on live data, automatically retrain when accuracy drops, and provide correctly-windowed training data. This is the core of MLOps.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

items.q: How does Grafana Loki achieve massive cost savings compared to Elasticsearch/Kibana for logs?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Loki does not index log line full text; it only indexes log metadata labels (e.g., service, env), storing compressed log chunks directly in object storage (S3/GCS), dramatically reducing storage and CPU costs.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Indexes store data in B-Tree structures. Clustered indexes dictate physical row storage on disk leaf pages; non-clustered indexes point to clustered keys or RIDs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Over-indexing degrades write performance on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations and leads to index fragmentation and page splits.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Covering indexes eliminate costly Key Lookups for read-heavy workloads but increase storage footprint and write transaction overhead.
